paragraphs.en: In Krowa, your task is to guess a Polish noun. A word is drawn at the start, and you are told how many letters it has. Enter guesses of the same length. After each attempt, you hear how many letters occupy the same positions in both words.

If the answer is kot and you enter sok, you get 1 out of 3: only the middle letter matches. K does not count, because it is first in kot but third in sok. Comparing these clues gradually narrows the search.
As the table host, you choose the game mode. There are two options for solo play:
- Daily Krowa: a new word every day, the same for everyone.
- Random word: words with a configurable number of letters.
Playing with others also offers two options:
- Race: compete to guess the same word. Depending on the setting, the winner is whoever uses fewer attempts or guesses faster.
- Word Tower: a cooperative game. Words are drawn and everyone takes turns entering guesses, seeing what the others have tried.
Daily Krowa is private: nobody can join or watch it. That would make guessing it later far too easy!

All the other modes can be watched if the table is open. If you join while someone is guessing a random word, you can check its length and the list and number of their attempts. You can also write in chat: “p in fourth place! Seriously, the fourth letter is p!” But I don't encourage it.

Random word mode gives you a superpower. You can add words to a dictionary that stores your nouns locally. Hmm... if you put asdfasdfasdf in there, it will store that too, but I'm counting on fun mattering more than padding leaderboard scores.

So if you want to enter smerfy as a guess, use the Add noun to dictionary and check button. You will not be able to use that word in Daily Krowa or the shared modes, though. And it isn't because I dislike Smurfs; the word simply isn't in the database.

Type a noun and press Enter. The input field clears after each submission. A wrong length, a word outside the dictionary, a repeat or an out-of-turn guess does not use an attempt, but does make a funny sound.
Daily Krowa can draw a word of three to nine letters. It follows server time, so if you need a different word, you'll have to break into the server and change the date.
You can open Daily Krowa only once each day. Whether you solve it, give up or leave the game unfinished, it remains unavailable to your account until the next day.

In a Race, everyone guesses independently. You can set a word length or leave it to chance. Either way, the host can draw a new word, which resets the attempts. The winning criterion mentioned earlier can also be set:
- By time: the shortest time from the start of the word to a correct answer wins, measured using a clock synchronised with the server.
- By attempts: the fewest accepted guesses needed to solve the word wins.
Equal results mean a shared win.
If everyone else has finished and you can no longer match the best result, the game ends and the word is revealed.
In the Tower, you take turns. Solving a word starts the next round. Words have 3 to 8 letters, and the shared attempt limit depends on their length:
- 3 letters: 15 attempts.
- 4 letters: 24 attempts.
- 5 letters: 30 attempts.
- 6 letters: 42 attempts.
- 7 letters: 49 attempts.
- 8 letters: 64 attempts.
The Tower ends when the attempts run out or the host gives up. Your score is the number of completed rounds. The round list in the leaderboard shows the words and attempt counts.
Krowa's music and effects start switched off. Ctrl+P opens their switches and separate volume controls. These sounds also follow Power Games' shared game-sound volume and mute settings.
The gallery remembers words you solved on your own and your best attempt count for each. You can open it before or after a game.

Its menu lets you sort by date, attempt count or length. Selecting a word with Enter opens its leaderboard. After a game, you can agree to publish your result, which also opens that word's leaderboard.

Leaderboards in the main menu provides word results and Word Tower round totals. The gallery and personal dictionary are local and separate for each account. To delete your own words, open Personal dictionary in Krowa settings, mark them with Space and choose Delete selected.

The host can save a Race or Word Tower while a word is being guessed, once all submitted guesses have been checked. An account save lets you resume with the same players at a new table. Solo games cannot be saved for later.
Krowa was created by paulinux.
Enter in the answer field: check the noun you typed.
Ctrl+P: open Krowa's sound and personal dictionary settings.
